episode_title: How to get better work from your SEO agency

real_qa.q: Should in-house brands default to bringing in SEO and marketing agencies or keep functions internal?
real_qa.r: Paddy Moogan argues that brands should not default to agencies and should try to keep as much as possible in-house first. He believes the biggest value agencies consistently bring now is decision confidence—helping with big strategic calls by lending the context and wider experience of having worked with dozens of clients across different industries. The consultative approach of lending that expertise is where agencies continue to add the most value, particularly in situations like salt migrations where an agency that has done 20 migrations can warn about obscure issues.
real_qa.requete: when should brands hire SEO agency vs in-house

real_qa.q: How do AI-native junior employees differ in value compared to traditional junior hires in marketing and SEO?
real_qa.r: Junior people coming into the workplace who are AI-native or AI-first have inherent advantage because they understand how these tools work from day one. This means they bring more than just task execution—they can contribute at a higher level than previous generations of juniors. Those who embrace AI and can demonstrate real competence with tools like Claude and ChatGPT, combined with the thinking and logic behind their solutions, can stand out and potentially become the middle-level and senior people of tomorrow, though agencies need to ensure they're not just hollowing out junior work through AI or budget constraints.
real_qa.requete: AI native junior employees SEO marketing agencies

real_qa.q: How does executive turnover and personnel changes impact agency-brand relationships?
real_qa.r: When CMOs or VPs of marketing change at brands, there is often an immediate assumption that the incumbent agency will be replaced. Paddy noted that at his agency Aira, they experienced two major client losses in 2023 when both clients had CMO and VP of marketing changes around the same time. While this is part of agency life that must be accepted, the power dynamic can be problematic if the new executive brings in an agency they already know, making the incumbent feel they must prove value all over again even if they were performing well.
real_qa.requete: CMO change agency relationship business impact

real_qa.q: What is the six-month plateau in agency-brand relationships and how should in-house teams address it?
real_qa.r: There is a predictable plateau around month five or six in agency relationships. Most good agencies deliver exceptional work in the first two to four months, but then things can become normalized and settled. Paddy recommends that in-house teams push through this point by freshening things up and ensuring the agency continues looking at the account in a fresh way, warning that recurring meetings can make both sides become too comfortable and complacent.
real_qa.requete: agency relationship six month plateau how to maintain quality

real_qa.q: Why are founders more naturally comfortable experimenting with AI and prompt engineering than traditional employees?
real_qa.r: Founders engage with AI more quickly because they have experience asking teams of humans to do things and implement systems. When they use AI, they recognize how much faster and more efficiently they could have built companies 10 or 20 years ago with these tools, which ignites passion and curiosity. The same person who might delegate to a human with a one-line request will happily write five pages of context for prompt engineering with AI because they're more patient and it feels quicker in terms of elapsed time, unlike waiting for email responses.
real_qa.requete: why founders use AI prompt engineering better than employees
